Layout text box rendering and legacy editor verification

Verified failure stages

The regression fixture models a black initial P, subsequent white letters, a bold accented second line and an additional coloured run. It also includes vendor metadata that the native rich-text handler cannot round-trip. The wxWidgets text buffer, extracted runs, HarfBuzz composition and FreeType outlines contain every supported letter. The preview raster test checks ink inside each glyph's bounds and checks the transparent counter inside the O.

On the baseline, the editor put white letters on its white editing surface. Opening the dialog also caused its first native layout to normalize the buffer after the application had recorded its XML baseline. Accepting the untouched dialog could therefore serialize the normalized buffer with a recovery copy. The editor now lays out the native buffer before taking its snapshot. Both the editor and the shared preview/PDF pipeline normalize legacy foreground colors to black in memory. Text boxes edited with the new controls store an optional useRichTextColors flag so explicitly chosen colors survive save/reopen. The editor gives light ink contrast on a neutral canvas when such colors are used.

The Layout texture upload divided edge RGB by alpha even though wxImage already exposes straight RGB. That raised the RGB values of translucent coloured edges before GL blended them. The renderer now initializes an image surface with explicit background pixels, completes the graphics context before reading the image and copies its straight RGB and alpha to the texture. This also avoids using a selected memory bitmap as the GDI+ alpha target on Windows.

The automated fixture reproduces the editor and texture handling conditions. The Windows screenshots show white legacy text after the initial black P, consistent with the mixed foreground colors in the regression fixture. An explicitly chosen white foreground needs contrast in the Layout or PDF. The reported Windows CacheOverflowException requires a native call stack to identify the throwing component.

Windows verification

Run the native GUI test from the repository with the Windows Debug dependencies installed.

cmake --preset win-x64-debug-ninja
cmake --build --preset win-debug-build-ninja --target layout_export_input_test
ctest --test-dir build/win-x64-debug-ninja -R "^LayoutExportInput$" --output-on-failure

For an end-to-end check in the application, export a Layout containing a text box as a JSON template. Replace its layouts[0].textViews[0].richText with the literal XML in tests/support/legacy_layout_text_fixture.h. Give it an area of at least 280 × 120 document points and omit useRichTextColors. Import the template with a transparent text background over the light page. Check that both lines are black in the Layout, Edit Text and Document preview. The old recovery notice should be absent. Cancel and reopen, then accept without edits. Both operations should retain the template's exact XML and leave project history alone.

Select a few letters and choose a color. Append a letter at the end of the second line, confirm, and verify Undo and Redo. Save and reopen the PSTG, then export the Layout as PDF. The edited XML contains the supported runs and one recovery comment containing the original XML. The Layout and PDF agree on the chosen color and keep the other runs black. Repeat with explicitly chosen white ink on a dark area and with an opaque white box using dark ink.
